newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso to slide less than 12 pct in '97-study.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso to slide less than 12 pct in '97-study.

text.p: The Mexican peso will slide by less than 12 percent against the dollar in 1997, ending the year at about 8.63 or 8.64 per dollar, a private sector study released Tuesday said.
The average exchange rate in 1997 would thus be about 8.24 pesos per dollar, the study said.

"With regard to the exchange rate, we estimate that on average it will be 8.24 pesos (per dollar)," Raymundo Winkler, director of the Center of Economic Studies of the Private Sector (CEESP), told an import-export conference.
"At the end of the period (of 1997) we will close at 8.63, 8.64 pesos per dollar, a devaluation of less than 12 percent."
The Mexican government's 1997 budget is based on an assumption of an average exchange rate of 8.53 pesos per dollar in the year.
The peso closed at 7.7980/7.8010 per dollar in its key 48-hour contract Tuesday.
Winkler also said the CEESP study predicted economic growth of 4.8 percent in 1997, inflation of about 17.4 percent and growth of aggregate demand of about 6.7 percent.
Total consumer demand would grow about 3.2 percent, he added.
Real average salaries would rise by between 2.5 and 3.5 percent and the current account deficit would be about $5 billion after two years of virtual balance, he said.
